FULL TEXT:
THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT
NEW INITIATIVES, SPECIAL ACCOMPLISHMENTS AND BEST PRACTICES
OF THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT
DURING THE TENURE OF
HON’BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. JUSTICE ARAVIND KUMAR
FROM 13-10-2021 TO 10-02-2023
ALSO AS
CHAIRMAN, INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (I.T.) COMMITTEE,
PATRON-IN-CHIEF OF
GUJARAT STATE LEGAL SERVICES AUTHORITY (GSLSA) &
GUJARAT STATE JUDICIAL ACADEMY (GSJA)
AND
CHAIRMAN OF VARIOUS OTHER ADMINISTRATIVE COMMITTEES
1. Arrears Reduction:
a. District Judiciary:
i. Monitoring work of 50 Years old Cases was undertaken for
speedy disposal and due to that, the age of pendency has
been reduced to 40 years old cases.
ii. Fortnightly Monitoring of pendency of MACP cases in various
Courts of the State which are pending for more than 10 years,
5-10 years and less than 5 years.
iii. Personal level hard work of monitoring and follow up by
Hon’ble the Chief Justice for oldest pending cases of District
Judiciary, resulted into sharp decrease of 20 years, 30
years and 40 years old cases. A detailed analysis with
charts is enclosed herewith for ready reference.
iv. Hon’ble the Chief Justice made very effective and efficient
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 1 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
utilization of the resources of SCMS War Room for report
generation and analysis of pendency, arrears and disposal
of cases of District Judiciary. A video of the visit of Hon’ble
the Chief Justice to the War Room along with details of
functionalities of the War Room has been prepared and will
be circulated separately.
b. High Court:
i. To reduce/minimize the pendency of cases in the High Court
of Gujarat, as per the orders of the Hon’ble Chief Justice,
ordinary pending matters registered upto-2005 including
connected matters, are being notified before the Honourable
Courts as per roster w.e.f. 01.08.2022. On being listed such
matters upto year 2005 before the Hon’ble Courts, 295
matters have been disposed of during the period from
01.08.2022 to 09.02.2023.
ii. Moreover, pending matters upto year 2001 pertaining to
Single Judge/Division Bench have been specially assigned
to four Honourable Courts (2 Division Benches and 2 Single
Judges) in the List of Sitting itself for early adjudication of
these matters.
iii. Special drives initiated:
1. As per the decision taken at the Honourable Chamber
Meeting held on 18.11.2022, approximately 775 Single
Judge First Appeals relating to MACP cases had been
assigned to 16 Hon’ble Courts (Single Judge) as
determined by the Hon’ble the Chief Justice and the same
were listed before the Hon’ble Courts for adjudication on
Wednesday, 14.12.2022. Out of which 203 First Appeals
relating to MACP cases have been disposed of by the
Hon’ble Courts till 01.02.2023.
2. Further, upon the directions of the Honourable the Chief
Justice, 87 First Appeals filed under Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 pertaining to Single Judge, having claim amount
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 2 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
(liability challenged) value up to Rs. 1,00,000/-, were
listed before the Hon’ble Courts on 13.01.2023 and
17.01.2023 and all 87 First Appeals were disposed of.
Further, 1338 First Appeals (Single Judge) were listed on
07.02.2023 before the Hon’ble Court (Coram : Hon’ble
the Chief Justice Mr.Justice Aravind Kumar), out of
which 1042 First Appeals have been disposed of by the
Hon’ble Court.
3. Provision in the List of Sitting had been made for listing
of cases which are more than 5 years old. All cases
which are more than 5 years old, have already been
Marked with the Stamp of “More than 5 years old” and
“Priority” on File Cover of the Judicial matters.
iv. Auto Listing of Fresh Matters: As per the direction of
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Mr. Justice Aravind Kumar, Auto
Listing within 2 / 3 days of filing, of the following categories
certain categories of fresh matters was implemented on pilot
basis from 07th July, 2022 onwards:
1. Regular Bail [Criminal Misc. Applications and Criminal
Appeals under The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled
Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989]
2. Anticipatory Bail [Criminal Misc. Applications and
Criminal Appeals under The Scheduled Castes and the
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989]
3. Quashing Petitions [Criminal Misc. Applications u/s. 482
of CrPC and Special Criminal Applications u/a. 226/227
of the Constitution r/w sec. 482 of CrPC]
2. Information & Communication Technology (ICT) Achievements:
Under the stewardship of Honourable the Chief Justice, the
Information Technology Cell has made the following major
developments from 13/10/2021 to 10/02/2023:
a. Complete, Accurate, Regular and Efficient (CARE) data
updation Guidelines for the Case Information System (CIS):
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 3 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
For ensuring quality, completeness and authenticity of the data
entered in Case Information System (CIS), Hon’ble the Chief
Justice formulated these guidelines called as CARE guidelines
which has yielded considerable results facilitating more accurate
report generation being done at War Room.
b. Infrastructure & Resource Information System (IRIS) platform
for convenient collection of information from all the Court
Establishments of the State:
i. To avoid regular practice of emailing for seeking various kind
of informations from the District Judiciary of the state, by
various department of High Court of Gujarat, & then
compiling all mails and extracting information at one place, a
new web based software module ‘Infrastructure & Resource
Information System (IRIS)’ has been developed by and hosted
at the IT Cell of the High Court of Gujarat. It is meant for
quick information collection, from the District Judiciary of the
state. This application eases the process of information
seeking, live follow up, final gathering & compilation of
received information as end result.
ii. This new software has saved hundreds of man hours of the
High Court Registry erstwhile used for manual compilation of
the information received through emails.
c. Expansion of Email My Case Status (EMCS) Service to Police,
Jails, DLSAs, Government Departments:
i. For the concerned Police Stations: Based on the entry of
FIR details for the cases of the High Court as well as the
District/Taluka Courts, automatic email transmission as part
of the Email My Case Status service has been implemented,
which is of immense use and benefit for the concerned Police
Stations in getting updates about the criminal cases and bail
applications etc.
ii. For Government Departments: Email My Case Status
service has also been extended for Government Departments
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 4 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
to avoid / restrict the time delay in execution of orders of the
Courts and also, to transmit updated instant information on
their registered emails, a modality document has been
implemented listing out the steps and measures to be taken
for facilitating registration of email addresses of the
Government Departments.
iii. For Legal Aided Cases: Email My Case Status services has
also been extended automatically for the cases wherein Legal
Aid has been taken for the ease of the stakeholders.
iv. For the Insurance Companies: Email My Case Status
sServices has also been extended automatically for the cases
wherein insurance companies are one of the parties.
d. Implementation of Online eCourt Fees platform for High
Court of Gujarat and District Judiciary:
i. Online eCourts Fee system for the High Court of Gujarat as
well as the District Judiciary of Gujarat was implemented
whereby Ld. Advocates / Parties can procure online the
Judicial Stamps through e-payment and submit a copy of the
PDF eCourt Fee Receipt in the Court. This platform is of M/s.
Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd. (SHCIL) as
empanelled by the Government of Gujarat.
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 5 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
ii. This eCourt Fees platform was inaugurated by Hon’ble Dr.
Justice D. Y. Chandrachud, Judge, Supreme Court of India
and Chairman, eCommittee, Supreme Court of India.
e. Justice Clock for High Court:
i. JUSTICE CLOCK is an Outdoor Display LED Video Wall to
work as ‘Justice Clock’ in the campus of the High Court of
Gujarat set up at a conspicuous place near a busy adjacent
cross-road (Kargil Petrol Pump) where optimum viewability is
expected.
ii. Gujarat High Court, along with this physical Justice Clock,
has also developed, as first of its kind initiative in the
country, its e-version i.e. virtual Justice Clock for the High
Court as well as all the Court establishment of the District
Judiciary of the State which is hosted on the High Court
website. The content being shown on the physical Justice
Clock shall be simultaneously shown on the virtual Justice
Clock page, thereby providing an online 24/7 access to
Justice Clock content to anyone and everyone without the
need to physically visit the High Court premises.
f. 39 Hi Speed Scanners procured for the High Court and District
Judiciary for Scanning Digitalization at the High Court and the
District Judiciary.
g. Equipment for Video Conferencing procured for all the Court
Rooms of the State.
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 6 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
h. 1250 Chromebook Touchscreen 2-in-1 Laptops purchased for
Judicial Officers with A. I. based Speech to text in English and
Gujarati.
i. Pilot Implementation of Live Streaming of Court Proceedings
of the Courts of Principal District Judges - Gujarat becoming
the first High Court and first State in the country to have
implemented live streaming of District Courts: Pilot
implementation of live streaming with recording of Court
Proceedings of Courts of all the Principal District Judges of the
State of Gujarat and Principal Judge, City Civil Court,
Ahmedabad, has been inaugurated by Honourable Mr. Justice M.
R. Shah, Judge, Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, in presence of
Hon’ble Mr. Justice J. B. Pardiwala, Judge, Supreme Court of
India, presided by Hon’ble the Chief Justice of the High Court of
Gujarat, Mr. Justice Aravind Kumar, on 08/02/2023.
j. Launch of Judicial Officers’ Portal: The Pilot implementation of
Judicial Officers’ Portal with eLeave, eACR, Property eReturns has
been inaugurated by Hon’ble Mr. Justice J. B. Pardiwala, Judge,
Supreme Court of India, in presence of Honourable Mr. Justice M.
R. Shah, Judge, Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, presided by
Hon’ble the Chief Justice of the High Court of Gujarat, Mr. Justice
Aravind Kumar, on 08/02/2023.
3. Two Day National Judicial Conference On Mediation And
Information Technology:
a. Based on the vision and guidance of Hon’ble the Chief Justice of
High Court of Gujarat Mr. Justice Aravind Kumar and the Hon’ble
Judges of the High Court of Gujarat, National Judicial Conference
was organized on 9th and 10th April, 2022, at the Tent City of
Kevadiya Colony, Near the Statue of Unity.
b. The Hon’ble the President of India Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji,
Hon’ble the Governor of Gujarat Shri Acharya Devavrat as well as
Hon’ble the Chief Justice of India Hon’ble Mr. Justice N.V.
Ramana graced the occasion of inauguration of the Conference.
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 7 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
c. Hon’ble the Chief Minister Shri Bhupendra Patel, Hon’ble Minister
for Law and Justice of Government of India Mr. Kiren Rijiju and
Hon’ble Mr. Justice L. Nageswara Rao, Hon’ble Mr. Justice S.
Abdul Nazeer, Hon’ble Mr. Justice M.R. Shah, Hon’ble Mr. Justice
Vikram Nath and Hon’ble Ms. Justice Bela M. Trivedi- Hon’ble
Judges of the Supreme Court attended the conference as special
guests of Honour and shared their thoughts and experiences on
the subjects with the invited dignitaries and delegates. This
conference was one of the largest congregations after the Covid-19
pandemic.
4. Human Resource Efficiency and Empowerment:
a. Judicial Officers’ Association: With the blessing, inspiration and
patronage of Hon’ble the Chief Justice Mr. Justice Aravind Kumar,
the association of Judicial Officers’ Association was revived and a
conference was held at Ahmedabad wherein more than 800
Judicial Officers had participated.
b. Judicial Officers’ Directory: Inauguration of Half-Yearly
Published Booklets of Hon’ble Judges and Judicial Officers of
the District Judiciary containing Service Details was done on
15.01.2022.
c. Departmental Proceedings against Judicial Officers’ and Staff
members:
i. Departmental Inquiries completed : 12
ii. Departmental Appeals completed : 33
iii. Suo Motu Reviews completed
including of years 2003, 2006,
2009, 2010 and 2011 : 15
d. Vigilance Applications and Inquiries:
i. No. of applications disposed off : 879
ii. No. of Preliminary Inquiry completed : 8
iii. No. of Discreet Inquiry completed : 5
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 8 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
iv. No. of Court Inquiries : 2
5. RECRUITMENT AND PROMOTION OF JUDICIAL OFFICERS AND
STAFF:
a. The task of printing of Question Paper of various Examinations
conducted by the Recruitment Cell in various Recruitment
Processes, has been undertaken in-house by the Recruitment
Cell, against the erstwhile practice of entrusting the said task to
the Confidential Agency. A Strong Room for in-house tasks was
inaugurated by the Honourable Chief Justice on 29/07/2022.
b. Scanning of OMR Sheets is also done in High Court premises
and Provisional Answer-Keys are uploaded on the date of exam
itself, within a couple of hours of Completion of examination for
enhanced transparency.
c. Newly recruited 55 Civil Judges were administered Oath by
the Honourable Chief Justice in presence of Honourable Judges
as well as the family members of Newly recruited Civil Judges on
06/02/2023 and this was the first of its kind function in the
history of Gujarat Judiciary. Identically, newly recruited District
Judge (25%) was also administered Oath by the Honourable Chief
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 9 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
Justice on 08/02/2023 in Committee Room No.1 in presence of
the Honourable Judges and his family members.
d. Further, the Recruitment Processes-2022 for the cadre of Civil
Judges, District Judge (25%) and District Judge(10%) were
concluded adhering to the Time-Schedule mentioned in the
Malik Mazhar Sultan case.
e. The High Court under its letter No.B.1458/79, dated
27/06/2022, directed all the Principal Judicial Officers to take
appropriate action to fill up vacant promotional posts in
various cadres within 35 days on their respective establishments,
and pursuant to the directions of the High Court, total 502
promotional posts of different cadres were filled up by the
concerned Principal Judicial Officers in the State.
f. Pursuant to the orders passed by the Honourable the Chief
Justice, vide High Court letter No.B.1424/78 dated 30/01/2023,
the Secretary to the Government of Gujarat was requested for
sanctioning and creating of total 3516 additional posts of
various cadres in the District Judiciary.
g. For conversion of temporary posts of District Judiciary of the
State into permanent posts, pursuant to the orders passed by the
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 10 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
Honourable the Chief Justice, vide High Court letter
No.A2401/2022, dated 01/02/2022, the Secretary to the
Government of Gujarat was requested for conversion of total 1199
temporary posts of District Judiciary of the State into permanent
posts. Out of which a total 420 temporary posts of Class 1 to
Class IV were converted into permanent.
h. During the period from 13-10-2021 to 09-02-2023, as per the
Government in General Administration Department Resolution
dated 07-07-2016, the proposals were forwarded by the District
Judiciary in the State as well as Industrial and Labour Court in
the State and accordingly, re-appointment on contractual basis
has been granted to total 21 Stenographers, being a technical
post, for smooth administration of District Judiciary in the State.
i. In the year 2022, the High Court of Gujarat has made the
proposal to the Government for sanctioning and creating a total
722 additional posts in the various cadres of Class-I to IV.
j. On recommendation of the Honourable the Chief Justice,
Government of Gujarat converted 7548 out of 12071
temporary posts of High Court as well as District Judiciary
into permanent posts.
k. Starting a novel welcome initiative, Oath ceremony of 55 newly
appointed Civil Judges and 1 Judicial Officer appointed in the
cadre of District Judge was conducted in the august presence of
Honourable Chief Justice and the Honourable Judges of the High
Court of Gujarat. This is the first time that Oath Ceremony of
newly appointed Judicial Officers was held in the High Court of
Gujarat and streamed on YouTube live for wide viewing
l. Various amendments were made in High Court of Gujarat
(Recruitment and Conditions of Service of Officers and Staff)
Rules 2011 to remove anomaly with regard to Service
Conditions for promotional avenues.
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 11 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
6. Court Complexes, Buildings and Residential Quarters
Infrastructure:
a. Under the leadership and guidance of Hon’ble the Chief Justice,
a high level coordination meeting was convened in the High
Court with Hon’ble the Chief Minister, Hon’ble Law Minister,
other Hon’ble Ministers and Secretaries of various Departments of
the Government of Gujarat,on 23.02.2022, various issues
pertaining to the State Judiciary were highlighted. Pursuant
thereto, initiatives were taken at all levels and several
developments have taken place.
b. Budgetary Allocation made / administrative approval given in
for:
i. Construction of a new Court building in the High Court
Campus - Rs. 8.28 Crore
ii. Additional Parking in the High Court Campus - Rs. 14
Crore
iii. Construction of New Administrative Building and Record
Room at High Court - Rs. 17.19 Crore [Administrative
approval accorded]
iv. Construction of New High Court Judges’ Guest House at
Dhuliakot - Rs. 12.56 Crore [Administrative approval
accorded]
v. Construction of connecting bridges between Court Rooms
- Rs. 84.23 Lacs [work completed on 31/12/2022]
c. Virtual Inauguration/Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony of
New District/Family/Taluka Court Buildings & Residence
Quarters for Judicial Officers and Staff Members was held on
22/10/2022.
7. Legal Aid and Services - GSLSA:
a. MEGA LEGAL SERVICE CAMP AT BHUJ, KACHCHH
(NOVEMBER-2021) AS PART OF PAN INDIA LEGAL AWARENESS
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 12 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
AND OUTREACH CAMPAIGN LAUNCHED BY NALSA,
INAUGURATED BY HON’BLE MR. JUSTICE UU LALIT:
b. MOOT COURT COMPETITION (NOVEMBER-2021) HELD AT
UNITEDWORLD SCHOOL OF LAW, UVARSAD,GANDHINAGAR:
c. LEGAL AWARENESS PROGRAMMES:
i. FOR JAIL INMATES (NOVEMBER-2021)
ii. SPECIAL LEGAL AWARENESS PROGRAMME IN
COLLABORATION WITH NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR
WOMAN (NOVEMBER-2021):
iii. LEGAL AWARENESS PROGRAMMES THROUGH RADIO
AAKASHWANI - AHMEDABAD & DOORDARSHAN,
AHMEDABAD (NOVEMBER-2021) WITH TALK SHOWS AND
INTERVIEWS:
d. SHORT PLAY DISSEMINATING INFORMATION REGARDING
AVAILABILITY OF LEGAL SERVICES (NOVEMBER-2021) IN
COLLABORATION WITH YOUTH AND CULTURAL DEPARTMENT
OF THE STATE GOVERNMENT:
e. 40 HOURS MEDIATION TRAINING PROGRAMME FOR JUDICIAL
OFFICERS AND ADVOCATES (NOVEMBER - 2021): under the
aegis of Mediation & Conciliation Project Committee (MCPC),
Supreme Court of India, New Delhi,
f. RECOMMENDATION OF RELEASING THE JAIL INMATES ON
INTERIM BAIL/PAROLE/ FURLOUGH DURING 3RD WAVE OF
PANDEMIC (JANUARY-2022): Total 628 prisoners were released
on interim bail /temporary bail /parole/furlough upon the
recommendation of GSLSA.
g. WEBINARS (FEBRUARY – 2022):
i. Mr.Justice K.N.Phaneendra, Former Judge, High Court of
Karnataka on the subject of ‘Role of Secretaries in
functioning of Legal Services Institutions’ for the
Secretaries of DLSAs/Committees across the State.
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 13 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
ii. For Panel Advocates, associated with various DLSAs and High
Court Legal Services Committee, a Webinar was organized on
5th February, 2022, on the subject of ‘Intricacies of
Sessions Trial and Criminal Appeals and Role of Legal Aid
Advocates’. Senior Advocate, High Court of Gujarat,
Mr.J.M.Panchal was invited to share his experience with 165
Panel Advocates of State.
h. ROAD SURVEY OF AHMEDABAD CITY (FEBRUARY – 2022):
Pursuant to the order passed on 24.01.2022 by the Hon’ble High
Court of Gujarat in Misc. Civil Application No. 979 of 2019,
directing the Member Secretary, GSLSA, and Secretary, DLSA
Ahmedabad Rural, to conduct a survey of roads and footpaths’
condition of Ahmedabad city. Member Secretary, GSLSA and
Secretary, DLSA Ahmedabad Rural, with the help of PLVs on a
pro-bono basis, constituted teams of PLVs to take visits of various
road sites situated in 07 different zones of Ahmedabad Municipal
Corporation. Thereafter, the various routes of roads were finalized
with the help of NGOs, Petitioner and his advocate and PLVs for
inspection. Then the teams of PLVs inspected a range of road sites
during 12th to 24th February, 2022 and filled up the forms of
reporting (proforma) with requisite comments and submitted the
same along with photographs. Later, the comment reports (in
proforma) submitted by PLVs were compiled by Member
Secretary, GSLSA and a detailed report (564 pages) was filed on
25th February, 2022 before the High Court.
i. INTERVIEW-CUM-TALK SHOW ON DOORDARSHAN FOR
SPREADING AWARENESS FOR LOK ADALAT (FEBRUARY – 2022)
BY THE THEN EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN OF GSLSA
j. ‘SIGNAL SCHOOL BUS’ – ‘FLAG OFF’ -
i. An event of launching of “Signal School Bus” was organized
by the Government of Gujarat, Gujarat State Legal Services
Authority, Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation & Municipal
School Board, on 6th March, 2022 at Gujarat High Court
Auditorium, Sola, Ahmedabad. On this day, total 10 Signal
New Initiatives, Special Accomplishments & Best Practices adopted during tenure of Page 14 / 20
Hon’ble the Chief Justice Shri Aravind Kumar from 13-10-2021 to 10-02-2023
School Buses were flag-off with the auspicious hands of
Hon’ble Chief Minister Mr. Bhupendrabhai Patel, in the
august presence of Hon’ble Mr. Justice M.R.Shah, Judge,
Supreme Court of India, Hon’ble Ms. Justice Bela M. Trivedi,
Judge, Supreme Court of India, Hon’ble Mr. Justice Aravind
Kumar, Chief Justice, High Court of Gujarat, Hon’ble Mr.

a. Achievements:
i. Post the Corona pandemic, the Gujarat State Judicial
Academy was first to resume the training from the virtual
training mode.

Academy has been accomplished. If the trainings are
compared with the working days in a month, the trainings far
exceed the working days.

their respective retirement.

proposal has been forwarded to the State Government for
approval.
